The \(f\)-divergence geometry over \(\mathcal P(\mathcal Y)\) attached to a fixed propensity \(e\in(0,1)\) with likelihood-ratio cap \(c=1/e\). Generators \(f\) range over the finite continuous convex functions \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\); the divergence is \(D_f(P\|Q)=\int_{\mathcal Y}f(dP/dQ)\,dQ\), taken as an extended-real quantity in \([0,+\infty]\), and the calibrated radius is \(B_f(e)=ef(1/e)+(1-e)f(0)\). The extended reading is forced and harmless: when \(P\ll Q\) the likelihood ratio \(r=dP/dQ\) satisfies \(\int r\,dQ=1\), and convexity gives a subgradient \(b\) at \(1\) with \(f(t)\ge b(t-1)\), so the negative part of \(f(r)\) is dominated by \(|b|(r+1)\) and is always \(Q\)-integrable; the integral is therefore always well defined, is nonnegative by Jensen, and equals \(+\infty\) exactly when \(f(r)\) fails to be \(Q\)-integrable. A divergence constraint \(D_f(P\|Q)\le B_f(e)\) is thus in particular an integrability requirement on the pair \((P,Q)\), and an arbitrary admissible generator supplies no integrability by itself. Distinguished generators are the Kullback--Leibler generator \(f_{\mathrm{KL}}(t)=t\log t\), the propensity hinge \(f_c(t)=(t-c)_+\), and the propensity-adaptive family \(f_e(t)=(t-1/e)_+\); the exactness frontier is the affine-equivalence class \(\mathfrak H_c\). nl.statement: One global nonparametric latent-variable SCM has observed vertices \(X,A,Y\), observed arrows \(X\to A\), \(X\to Y\), and \(A\to Y\), and a latent variable \(U\) that may be a parent of each of \(X,A,Y\).
nl.frozen_body:
The conditional model is a single global nonparametric latent-variable SCM witness with common conditional objects. It consists of a probability law on the covariate and outcome measurable-space carrier product \(\mathcal X\times\{0,1\}\times\mathcal Y\times\mathcal Y\), with coordinates \((X,A,Y(0),Y(1))\), an observed-outcome selector \(Y\), a covariate probability law \(\mu_X\), real-valued arm functions \(\boldsymbol e=(e_0,e_1)\), observed arm-law Markov kernels \(\boldsymbol P=(P_0,P_1)\), and interventional Markov kernels \(\boldsymbol Q=(Q_0,Q_1)\). Probabilities below are computed under this joint law.
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Observed vertices.)} The observed vertices are the covariate \(X\), treatment \(A\), and outcome \(Y\).
\item \textbf{(Observed arrows.)} The observed directed edges are \(X\to A\), \(X\to Y\), and \(A\to Y\).
\item \textbf{(Latent parent.)} The global latent state \(U\) is represented by the latent coordinates in the joint tuple and may parent \(X\), \(A\), and \(Y\).
\item \textbf{(Law identities.)} For every measurable covariate set \(C\), every arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), and every measurable outcome set \(B\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
\Pr\{X\in C\} &= \mu_X(C),\\
\Pr\{X\in C,\ A=a\} &= \int_C^- (e_a(x))_+\,d\mu_X(x),\\
\Pr\{X\in C,\ A=a,\ Y\in B\} &= \int_C^- (e_a(x))_+\,P_a(x,B)\,d\mu_X(x),\\
\Pr\{X\in C,\ Y(a)\in B\} &= \int_C^- Q_a(x,B)\,d\mu_X(x).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here \(\int^-\) is the extended nonnegative integral and \((e_a(x))_+\) is the nonnegative part of \(e_a(x)\).
\end{itemize}

review.note: The joint law on (X,A,Y(0),Y(1)) is an equivalent saturated representation of the stated unrestricted latent-variable SCM, and the displayed identities merely require the carried propensity and observed/interventional kernels to be versions of its conditional laws on the standard-Borel consumer domain.

nl.statement: Let \(e_1,e_2\in(0,1)\) with \(e_1\ne e_2\). No single finite continuous convex generator \(f:[0,\infty)\to\mathbb R\) with \(f(1)=0\) is universally exact at both propensities: it is impossible to have \(\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e_i}(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_{e_i}(P)\) for every probability law \(P\) and both \(i=1,2\). Let \(e_1,e_2\) be distinct fixed propensities satisfying \cref{obj:ass:positivity}, so \(0<e_i<1\) for \(i=1,2\). Then:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(No shared finite generator.)} There is no finite generator \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) that is continuous on \([0,\infty)\), convex on \([0,\infty)\), normalized by \(f(1)=0\), and universally one-sided exact at both propensities, meaning that
\[
\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f,e_i}(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_{e_i}(P)
\]
for every standard Borel outcome space, every probability law \(P\) on that space, and both \(i=1,2\).
\item \textbf{(Disjoint hinge classes.)} The affine-equivalence hinge generator classes at the two caps are disjoint:
\[
\mathfrak H_{1/e_1}\cap\mathfrak H_{1/e_2}=\varnothing .
\]
\item \textbf{(Adaptive exactness.)} For every propensity \(e\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:positivity}, the adaptive hinge
\[
f_e(t)=(t-1/e)_+
\]
belongs to \(\mathfrak H_{1/e}\), is universally one-sided exact at \(e\), and is universally exact for the mutual-support divergence ball at \(e\). Equivalently, for every standard Borel outcome space and every probability law \(P\) on that space,
\[
\mathfrak B^{\to}_{f_e,e}(P)=\mathfrak L^{\to}_e(P),\qquad
\mathfrak B_{f_e,e}(P)=\mathfrak L_e(P).
\]
\end{itemize}

nl.statement: Fix \(0<e<1\) and \(0<\alpha<1/2\). Consider any sequence of rectangular simultaneous bands that has asymptotic coverage at least \(1-\alpha\) uniformly over a local class. Suppose the class contains a boundary observed-data law with \(F_P(y_0)=1\) and a sequence of alternatives with the same arm propensity \(e\) such that \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=1-\delta_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), where \(\delta_n>0\), \(n\delta_n\to0\), and the total-variation distance between the corresponding \(n\)-sample observed-data laws is \(o(1)\). Under the boundary law, with probability at least \(1-2\alpha-o(1)\), the lower-endpoint projection of the band at \(y_0\) has diameter at least \(1-e\). The analogous assertion holds for the upper-endpoint projection when the class contains a boundary law with \(F_P(y_0)=0\) and alternatives with the same propensity such that \(F_{P,n}(y_0)=\delta_n\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), under the same \(n\)-sample total-variation condition. Such alternative sequences, with the displayed CDF identities holding for all sufficiently large \(n\), exist within the bow-SCM class whenever \(\delta_n>0\) and \(n\delta_n\to0\). Consequently, \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{dir}}\) cannot yield a nonconservative shrinking band uniformly over such a total-variation-local tie-inclusive class; derivative-aware inference is restricted to strata separated from these contacts, with \(\widehat{\mathcal C}_{n,\alpha}\) retained as the honest fallback. The extension of \(L_e,U_e\) to \(e=0\) is algebraic and used only by the clipped finite-sample construction; this impossibility result assumes \(0<e<1\).

Fix \(e\) and \(\alpha\) with \(0<e<1\) as in \cref{obj:ass:positivity} and \(0<\alpha<1/2\).  Let \(B_n(S,y)\subseteq\mathbb R^2\) be a rectangular finite-sample simultaneous endpoint band, and let \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}\) be a local class of observed-data laws paired with their arm-CDF laws.  Assume that, for each \(n,y,z\), the event \(\{S:z\in B_n(S,y)\}\) is measurable, and that \(B\) has uniform asymptotic simultaneous coverage at level \(1-\alpha\) over \(\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}\).

For every arm \(a\in\{0,1\}\), contact side \(s\in\{0,1\}\), threshold \(y_0\), boundary arm law \(P_0\), alternative arm laws \(P_n\), gaps \(\delta_n\), boundary observed-data law \(\nu_0\), and alternative observed-data laws \(\nu_n\), suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Tie contact.)}  \(\nu_0\) is the bow-SCM observed law with arm \(a\), propensity \(e\), and arm law \(P_0\); for all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\nu_n\) is the corresponding bow-SCM observed law with arm law \(P_n\); \(F_{P_0}(y_0)=s\); and, writing \(F_{P_n}(y_0)\) for the CDF of the alternative arm law \(P_n\) at \(y_0\),
\[
F_{P_n}(y_0)=
\begin{cases}
1-\delta_n, & s=1,\\
\delta_n, & s=0
\end{cases}
\]
for all sufficiently large \(n\).
\item \textbf{(Local drift.)}  \(\delta_n>0\) for every \(n\), \(n\delta_n\to0\), and the \(n\)-sample product laws generated by \(\nu_0\) and \(\nu_n\) are total-variation local.
\item \textbf{(Membership and sampling.)}  \((\nu_0,P_0)\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}\), \((\nu_n,P_n)\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{loc}}\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), and the samples are iid as in \cref{obj:ass:iid-sampling} under the product laws generated by \(\nu_0\) and, eventually, by \(\nu_n\).
\end{itemize}
Then, under the boundary law \(\nu_0\),
\[
\Pr_{\nu_0^n}\!\left\{
\exists z_1,z_2\in B_n(S,y_0):
1-e\le
\begin{cases}
|z_{1,L}-z_{2,L}|, & s=1,\\
|z_{1,U}-z_{2,U}|, & s=0
\end{cases}
\right\}
